## Appearance

Marilla is a tall, thin, and gaunt woman defined by her angular frame. Her dark hair, which has grown grayer over time, is styled in a hard little knot secured with two wire hairpins. Though she often looks tired, her angular features are complemented by a softer expression on her face, and she is shorter in stature than [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md).

## Personality

A woman of rigid conscience and narrow experience, Marilla is a sensible, determined, and self-contained individual who often comes across as critical. While nature and habit render her reserved when it comes to expressing her deeper feelings, she can also become somewhat sarcastic after suffering from headaches. In her household management, she takes pride in her skills as a famous cook, celebrated for her homemade currant wine, and refuses to be surpassed by other local housekeepers. As a guardian, she views it as her duty to drill [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) into a tranquil uniformity of disposition, while remaining dedicated to providing her with a good education that will enable her to earn her own living.

## History

Marilla Cuthbert lived a conservative, relatively easy life at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) alongside her brother [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md), having once quarreled with John Blythe in her past and refused to forgive him. Her quiet household was upended when [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) brought home an orphan girl, [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md), instead of the boy they had intended to adopt to help on the farm. Though initially set on sending [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) back, Marilla took pity on the child's tragic past and agreed to keep and raise her. Marilla strictly managed Anne's religious upbringing and discipline, though she steadily developed a deep, quiet maternal affection for the girl. When [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) accidentally served currant wine to [Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md), Marilla attempted to intercede with Diana's mother, and she later supported [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) through various childhood mishaps, from a missing brooch misunderstanding to cropped green hair. As [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) grew older, Marilla and [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) agreed to pay for her extra studies in Miss Stacy's Queen's [Entrance](../codex/places.md#entrance) class so she could train as a teacher. After [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) tied for first place on the island and left for Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy), Marilla proudly watched her win the Avery scholarship. However, [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) died suddenly of a heart attack following a bank failure, leaving Marilla to grieve alongside [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md). When an oculist informed Marilla that her failing eyesight meant she must give up reading and sewing or risk total blindness, she prepared to sell [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables). [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) promptly gave up her college scholarship to stay home, care for Marilla, and teach at the local school, securing their future together at the farm.

## Quotes

> "No. We want a boy to help Matthew on the farm. A girl would be of no use to us. Take off your hat. I’ll lay it and your bag on the hall table."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised P30](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0030)

> "Well, undress as quick as you can and go to bed. I’ll come back in a few minutes for the candle. I daren’t trust you to put it out yourself. You’d likely set the place on fire."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised P44](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0044)

> "I don’t feel as if I wanted any more children to look after than I’ve got at present. You’re problem enough in all conscience. What’s to be done with you I don’t know. Matthew is a most ridiculous man."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER IV. Morning at Green Gables P25](../source/v01-c04.md#nw-v01-c04-p0025)

> “There, there, Marilla, you can have your own way,” said Matthew reassuringly. “Only be as good and kind to her as you can without spoiling her. I kind of think she’s one of the sort you can do anything with if you only get her to love you.”
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER VI. Marilla Makes Up Her Mind P35](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0035)

> "I suppose we could, but we decided not to. Matthew took a fancy to her. And I must say I like her myself—although I admit she has her faults. The house seems a different place already. She’s a real bright little thing."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Properly Horrified P9](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0009)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--marilla-cuthbert.md)

Marilla took [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) in as an orphan by mistake, initially planning to send her back before deciding to adopt and raise her alongside [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md). She acts as a strict yet increasingly affectionate mother and mentor, guiding [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) in her household chores, manners, and religious education. Though Marilla frequently finds herself having to discipline [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) for her dramatic outbursts and stubbornness, she grows to feel a deep, genuine affection for the girl.

- Parent of — adoptive mother  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XXIX. An Epoch in Anne’s Life P32](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0032), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIV. A Queen’s Girl P19](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0019)</sub>
- Friend of — close, trusted friend who raised her  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XXXI. Where the Brook and River Meet P8](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0008)</sub>
- Mentor of — teaching her to cook  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XVI. Diana Is Invited to Tea with Tragic Results P27](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0027)</sub>

### [Martin](../character/martin.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/marilla-cuthbert--martin.md)

Marilla holds authority over [Martin](../character/martin.md) as a household worker following the sudden death of her brother, [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md). After processing her grief with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and settling back into a routine, Marilla relies on [Martin](../character/martin.md) to manage farm duties while she faces her own health issues and prepares to see an eye specialist.

- Commands  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XXXVII. The Reaper Whose Name Is Death P28](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0028)</sub>

### [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/marilla-cuthbert--rachel-lynde.md)

Marilla and [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) are long-time neighbors and close, trusted friends who regularly visit and travel together. Although [Rachel](../character/rachel-lynde.md) frequently voices unsolicited opinions, skepticism, and unsolicited advice regarding Marilla's household decisions—such as adopting an orphan or raising [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md)—Marilla continues to turn to her for guidance during difficult parenting moments.
